memory_lessons.applicability: Terminal-power generation for this binomial kernel; the centered progression proposed here remains unmeasured.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured one-ended progression passed 8 controller cases with maximum reported absolute error 0.0002117156982421875 and mean time 0.30636386899657236 s, versus the baseline's 0.39007941525227696 s. Those results apply to that candidate and tested inputs, not to the centered progression.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Run the centered progression through the same varied-input correctness checks and performance protocol, then compare against both measured programs.

proposal.hypothesis: The prior one-ended progression was valid and faster than baseline, but still used a starting powf and accumulated powers along one chain. Anchoring at exponent zero (j=32) and generating the positive and negative exponents in separate geometric progressions removes terminal powf calls and limits each progression to 32 values. This tests whether the shorter, two-sided chains improve runtime or FP32 error; the controller must measure and validate this candidate.

retained: Replace the terminal powf calls with two geometric power progressions anchored at exponent zero: forward from j=32 using u squared and backward from j=31 using d squared.
Preserve the 64-value terminal array, j=0..63 terminal payoff indexing and expression, and backward recurrence order.
